note: Retrieves the year from the tm struct. For a timepoint with a very large Rep value, the year can exceed 10000, triggering the extended year path.
When year >= 10000, write_year_extended writes the year digits directly to out_, then year is reset to 0. The offset is set to 4 so that only the last 6 bytes of buf are copied later.
Writes the extended year digits to the output iterator. The output buffer grows as needed, so this is safe.
Writes 8 bytes to buf[2] through buf[9]. buf is char[10], so this is within bounds. The year was reset to 0, so year % 100 = 0.
Copies 6 bytes from buf[4] to buf[10] to out_. This is within bounds of buf. The output is: [year digits] + [MM-DD].

note: Writes 8 bytes to buf[0] through buf[7]. buf is char[8], so this is within bounds.
Copies 8 bytes from buf to out_. This is safe.
Computes the number of fractional digits for the duration period. For system_clock with nanosecond precision, this is 9.
Converts the fractional seconds to the subsecond precision. The value is used to write the fractional digits.
Converts subseconds to an unsigned value. If subseconds is negative (due to negative timepoint), to_nonnegative_int clamps it to 0.
Counts the number of digits in n. If n is 0, num_digits is 1.

note: Pads with leading zeros to reach num_fractional_digits total digits. This writes to out_ which is the output iterator.
Writes the actual digits to out_. The output buffer grows as needed, so this is safe.
Creates a tm struct with the hour value. If the hour is negative, it is clamped to 0.
Formats the tm struct using the on_24_hour callback. This recursively calls the tm_writer with the new tm.
Creates another tm struct with the hour value. This recursive call can happen multiple times if the hour is out of range.
Recursively formats the tm struct again. This can lead to infinite recursion if the hour value is always out of range, causing stack overflow.

The recursive call continues. The hour() function returns the hour from the tm struct, which was set to the clamped value. If the original hour was very large, the clamped value may still be out of range.
The recursion continues indefinitely, eventually causing a stack overflow. This is the root cause of the crash.
